EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Israel's political landscape faces significant instability with ultra-Orthodox parties threatening to dissolve the Knesset over the conscription law, while military operations in southern Lebanon intensify with IDF ground incursions and continued Hezbollah attacks. Concurrently, regional tensions remain extremely high with reports of covert Saudi and Emirati strikes on Iran, a Kuwaiti-Iran infiltration incident, and bellicose rhetoric from the US regarding potential renewed military action and Iran's uranium enrichment program.

IRAN
Saudi Arabia reportedly carried out several retaliatory airstrikes on Iran in late March. The UAE also conducted covert strikes, including an attack on an oil refinery on Iran's Lavan Island in early April. The IRGC's Greater Tehran Command conducted a large-scale military exercise for five days and nights, focusing on readiness for enemy confrontation. Iran executed Abduljalil Shahbakhsh, identified as a "terrorist trained" by the Ansar al-Furqan group.

Economically, the war has cost the US $29 billion so far, and US inflation rose to 3.8% in April. The UK faces 163,000 job losses due to the war's economic fallout. Oil prices are expected to remain above $100 for most of the year if the Strait of Hormuz reopens, potentially surging to $140-160 if severe damage occurs. Internet access in Iran continues to be restricted, leading to public discontent and the emergence of an unofficial market for Iraqi SIM cards and "Pro" internet services.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman outlined five conditions for negotiations with the US: an end to the war on all fronts (especially in Lebanon), the lifting of all sanctions, the release of frozen funds, compensation for war damages, and recognition of Iran's sovereign rights in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also officially filed a lawsuit against the US at The Hague Tribunal for "June 2025 aggression," demanding war reparations. The IRGC Navy declared an expanded 500-kilometer "operational crescent" in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting full control and warning against violations. Spokesman for Iran's National Security Committee threatened 90% uranium enrichment if the US renews attacks.

ISRAEL
Israeli ground forces from the Golani Brigade completed a week-long operation across the Litani River near Zawtar al-Sharqiyah in southern Lebanon, killing dozens of Hezbollah operatives in close-quarters combat and airstrikes, and locating Hezbollah tunnels, weapon depots, and rocket launchers. Several Israeli soldiers sustained minor injuries, and an Oketz canine unit dog was killed during the raid. In the past day, the IDF killed approximately 15 Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon and struck about 45 Hezbollah targets, including command centers, surveillance posts, staging grounds, and 10 weapon depots. Since the start of the ceasefire understandings, the IDF reports having killed over 350 Hezbollah operatives and struck more than 1,100 targets in southern Lebanon. In Gaza, the IDF killed at least four Palestinian terror operatives in northern and southern parts of the Strip.

A non-commissioned officer was moderately wounded, and a reservist lightly injured in a Hezbollah drone attack that struck Israeli territory near the Lebanon border. 8 Golani Brigade fighters were injured in three clashes near the Litani River.

Israeli air defenses engaged hostile aircraft intrusions, including explosive drones, across northern Israel, particularly in Margaliot, Manara, the Galilee Panhandle, Hurfeish, Alkosh, Matat, and Fassuta. Some drones were intercepted, others exploded on Israeli territory, and contact was lost with additional targets. The IDF also intercepted a drone "launched from the east" near Eilat, which is suspected to have originated from Yemen.

Domestically, a significant political crisis unfolded as ultra-Orthodox parties, specifically Dagel Hatorah, threatened to dissolve the Knesset and trigger new elections if a law exempting religious students from military service is not passed, citing a lack of trust in Prime Minister Netanyahu. The Knesset approved a law allowing for the prosecution of October 7 terrorists, including the possibility of a death penalty and no release in future hostage deals, passing with 93 votes. The European Union extended its recommendation against non-essential travel to Israel until May 27, impacting major European airlines.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinian terror operatives in northern and southern Gaza yesterday (May 11). The World Health Organization reported that 43,000 Gazans, including 10,000 children, have suffered life-threatening injuries during the Israeli war on Gaza. Hamas has reportedly refused to disarm or relinquish control in Gaza and threatened contractors working on a planned UAE-funded city in Rafah. The European Commission reiterated the existence of a proposal to ban products from Israeli settlements but declined to introduce a new one.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched rockets at Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon, with some intercepted and others falling in open areas. Multiple explosive drones and suspicious aerial targets were launched by Hezbollah towards Israeli forces and Israeli territory, with some intercepted and others detonating near the border. A surface-to-air missile fired by Hezbollah at an Israeli drone reportedly failed and caused no damage. Hezbollah forces also used loitering munitions to target Israeli soldiers in Taybeh, a military vehicle in Deir Suryan, and a house in Taybeh and Tyr Harfa. Two Lebanese civil security personnel were killed in an Israeli strike in Nabatiyeh, and six civilians were killed with seven injured in an overnight Israeli airstrike against a residential building in southern Lebanon.

In response to Hezbollah activities, the IDF killed approximately 15 operatives and struck about 45 targets, including command centers, surveillance posts, military buildings, and weapon depots. Israeli aircraft also struck a suspect on a motorcycle fleeing a missile launch site. The IDF issued evacuation warnings for the Lebanese villages of Arzoun, Tir Daba, al-Bazouriya, and al-Housh.

The first round of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel is scheduled to begin on Thursday at 16:00 Israel time, mediated by the US, whose Ambassador to Lebanon is expected to arrive in Washington for preparatory meetings. Hezbollah's Secretary-General stated that relinquishing weapons is not part of negotiations with Israel.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Ismail Qaani, commander of the Quds Force, visited Baghdad for security coordination amidst concerns over Iraq being drawn into the Iran-Israel conflict. Hashd al-Shaabi forces were deployed in the Najaf desert in western Iraq, searching for suspicious activity after the Iraqi Defense Ministry initially reported finding remnants of guided missiles and a suspected enemy base, although they later denied an airborne landing or base.

In the broader regional context, an explosion was reported in Sanaa, Yemen. Yemen has called on the UN to end the 10-year blockade by the US and its allies. US President Trump stated that there is no understanding with Russian President Putin that Russia would receive Donbas, and predicted that the war in Ukraine would end "very soon."

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia reportedly informed Iran in advance of its retaliatory strikes in late March, leading to intensive diplomatic contacts and a mutual understanding to reduce tensions. The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE secretly conducted strikes inside Iran, including on the Lavan Island refinery in early April. The UAE also placed 21 individuals and entities on its terrorism list for alleged links to Hezbollah and saw its largest gas processing plant suffer damage that may not be fully repaired until 2027. Israel secretly deployed Iron Dome missile-defense batteries and personnel to the UAE during the war with Iran.

Kuwait arrested four armed individuals allegedly affiliated with Iran's Revolutionary Guards who attempted to infiltrate by sea, resulting in injury to a Kuwaiti security forces member. Kuwait summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest the incident, though Iran's Foreign Ministry denied the claims, stating its citizens were on a routine naval patrol and experienced a navigation system malfunction. The Gulf Cooperation Council condemned alleged Iranian influence in Kuwait. Bahrain sentenced three individuals to life in prison for allegedly aiding Iran.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC Navy asserted an expanded 500-kilometer "operational crescent," warning against encroachments. The US prevented the Malta-flagged tanker "Agios Fanourios" from passing through the Strait, citing a violation of the blockade, despite the tanker not carrying Iranian oil. Maersk, the world's second-largest container shipping company, continues to avoid transit through the Strait. Oil prices are expected to remain elevated due to the situation. Turkey's Foreign Minister supports reopening the Strait, emphasizing it should not be used as a weapon. The UK pledged autonomous vessels, minehunting systems, Typhoon fighter jets, and the HMS Dragon warship for a multinational defensive mission to ensure free navigation. JPMorgan anticipates the Strait's reopening around June 11, with Goldman Sachs predicting a "gradual" reopening.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Israeli Political Crisis:** Ultra-Orthodox parties threatened to dissolve the Knesset over the stalled conscription law, signaling a potential collapse of the governing coalition and new elections.
2.  **Hezbollah-Israel Border Escalation:** A non-commissioned officer was moderately wounded and a reservist lightly hurt in a Hezbollah drone attack near the Lebanon border. The IDF killed 15 Hezbollah operatives and struck 45 targets, while conducting a week-long ground operation across the Litani River, killing dozens more.
3.  **Covert Strikes on Iran:** Reuters reported Saudi Arabia carried out "several strikes" in Iran in late March, and the Wall Street Journal reported the UAE secretly conducted strikes on Iran, including the Lavan Island oil refinery, in early April.
4.  **Kuwaiti Infiltration Incident:** Kuwait arrested four armed individuals allegedly linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards attempting to infiltrate by sea, leading to an injury of a Kuwaiti security member and a diplomatic protest with Iran.
5.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** Iran's IRGC Navy declared an expanded 500-kilometer "operational crescent" in the Strait, while the US prevented a Malta-flagged tanker from passing due to a "blockade violation." The UK committed military assets to a multinational mission to ensure free navigation.
6.  **Iran's Negotiation Demands:** Iran formally outlined five conditions for starting negotiations with the US: end the war, lift sanctions, release frozen funds, compensation for damages, and recognition of sovereignty in the Strait of Hormuz.
7.  **US Military Posture and War Costs:** A Pentagon official stated the war with Iran has cost the US $29 billion so far, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth indicated plans for escalation if necessary, despite also affirming the ceasefire is in effect.
8.  **Iran's Nuclear Threat:** A spokesman for Iran's National Security Committee threatened 90% uranium enrichment if the US renews attacks.
9.  **Knesset Approves Terrorist Prosecution Law:** The Knesset passed a law to prosecute October 7 terrorists, allowing for the death penalty and prohibiting their release in future hostage deals.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain extremely high, particularly between Israel and Hezbollah, with continued cross-border attacks and deeper IDF ground operations into southern Lebanon. Iran's threat to enrich uranium to 90% if attacked by the US constitutes a significant red line, while President Trump's contemplation of resuming "major combat operations" against Iran suggests a potential shift towards renewed hostilities. The ongoing dispute over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's expanded operational claims and US enforcement of blockades, alongside increased military presence from the UK, poses a constant risk of naval confrontation and disruption to global energy supplies. The Kuwaiti infiltration incident also adds to regional instability and the potential for miscalculation. Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, the Strait of Hormuz, and, to a lesser extent, Gaza. Military posture changes indicate an overall readiness for escalation from multiple actors.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture remains assertive, with President Trump rejecting Iran's latest negotiation proposal, expressing confidence that Iran will cease uranium enrichment, and hinting at finishing the job if Iran does not cooperate. The Pentagon cited a $29 billion cost for the war and affirmed plans for escalation if needed, while a US nuclear submarine arrived in Gibraltar.

Among Gulf States, Saudi Arabia engaged in diplomatic contacts with Iran to reduce tensions and reportedly carried out covert strikes. The UAE also conducted covert strikes on Iran and designated 21 Hezbollah-linked entities as terrorists. Qatar's Foreign Minister advocated for stability and warned Iran against weaponizing the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait arrested alleged IRGC infiltrators and formally protested to Iran, which Iran denied. Bahrain sentenced individuals for aiding Iran.

EU members demonstrated mixed responses: the EU extended its travel advisory for Israel, while the European Commission declined a new proposal to ban settlement products. Germany expressed reluctance to support the US war against Iran. Russia's President Putin announced successful tests of the Sarmat ICBM and advanced work on other nuclear systems, while also progressing plans for a visit to China and expanding its drone factory with Iran. China rejected Israeli allegations of missile support for Iran and emphasized de-escalation, playing a balancing role for Iran. Turkey's Foreign Minister prioritized maintaining the US-Iran ceasefire and supported Pakistan's mediation efforts. The UK pledged autonomous vessels, fighter jets, and a destroyer to a multinational mission for securing the Strait of Hormuz.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions exist between Iraqi Defense Ministry reports on a suspected enemy base in Najaf desert and subsequent denials. Conflicting accounts from Kuwait and Iran regarding the alleged IRGC infiltration incident in Kuwaiti waters highlight the difficulty in verifying events in politically charged environments. US Defense Secretary Hegseth's assertion that the ceasefire with Iran remains in effect appears at odds with President Trump's contemplation of renewed military operations. Trump's claim that Iranians offered to hand over enriched material conflicts with Iran's recent threat of 90% enrichment. Propaganda indicators are evident in Press TV's framing of the conflict and Trump's rhetoric and social media posts. Reporting gaps include specific details of Saudi and UAE strikes, full casualty counts from Israel-Hezbollah exchanges, and the precise nature of the "Yellow Line" in Gaza.
